intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes memory consistency issues for non-coherent IOMMUs by flushing the CPU cache after allocating PASID entries.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check for non-coherent IOMMU capability followed by a call to clflush_cache_range on the allocated entries buffer.
intent_record.how: Ensures CPU cache is flushed to main memory before the IOMMU accesses the newly allocated PASID entry, preventing stale data reads on non-coherent hardware.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect cache flush target by changing from entries array to directory entry when IOMMU coherence is disabled
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional block wrapping clflush_cache_range(entries, VTD_PAGE_SIZE) and replaced it with clflush_cache_range(&dir[dir_index].val, sizeof(*dir)) under the same ecap_coherent() condition check
intent_record.how: Changes which memory region gets cache flushed when IOMMU coherence is not enabled - now flushes the directory entry instead of the entries array, ensuring correct cache coherency for the actual data being modified

grouping_result.intent: Fix incorrect cache flush target by changing from entries array to directory entry when IOMMU coherence is disabled

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix incorrect cache flush target and ensure memory consistency for non-coherent IOMMUs during PASID allocation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement handles PASID table entry allocation validation. In the context of IOMMU PASID table operations, improper handling of entries allocation can lead to race conditions or memory consistency issues when concurrent IOMMU operations occur. The cache coherency management (clflush_cache_range) following this allocation is critical for preventing stale data issues in multi-core systems.
